title: Entropy-Driven Altermagnetism from Thermal Magnons
authors: Tanaya Halder, Ashis K. Nandy, Anamitra Mukherjee
abstract: We identify a route to altermagnetism driven by entropy upon heating and demonstrate it in a minimal square-lattice antiferromagnet. An exchange modulation is entropically favored because the resulting momentum-dependent magnon splitting increases the magnon entropy, thereby lowering the free energy and favoring altermagnetism. We derive an instability criterion for this exchange-modulated state, predict its temperature-driven reentrant behavior, and show that its overlap with Néel order defines a finite-temperature altermagnetic phase. Variational spin-wave theory, spin--lattice Monte Carlo, and cluster diagonalization establish the entropy-driven instability and its coexistence with magnetic order. The resulting state supports a transverse spin conductivity. The mechanism provides a route to thermally induced altermagnetism in compensated magnets coupled to sufficiently soft physical modes.
summary: This work demonstrates that altermagnetism can be thermally induced in antiferromagnets through an entropy-driven instability in the exchange coupling. By showing that the entropic gain from magnon excitation favors an exchange modulation ($\delta$), the authors establish a finite-temperature phase where the system exhibits altermagnetic properties, measurable via transverse spin conductivity.
main_problem: The paper identifies a mechanism where entropy, rather than symmetry breaking, drives the emergence of altermagnetism in an antiferromagnet upon heating.
main_result: The system enters a finite-temperature altermagnetic phase characterized by an exchange modulation ($\delta$) when the entropic gain overcomes the energetic cost, leading to a non-zero transverse spin conductivity.
method: The study employs variational spin-wave theory, spin-lattice Monte Carlo simulations, and cluster diagonalization to analyze the free energy landscape.
model_or_system: The model is a minimal square-lattice antiferromagnet with nearest-neighbor and next-nearest-neighbor exchange interactions, incorporating an exchange modulation ($\delta$).
key_observables: Altermagnetism (momentum-dependent spin splitting), free energy difference ($\Delta f$), transverse spin conductivity ($\sigma_{zxy}/	au$), and the equilibrium modulation $\delta^*(T)$.
important_parameters: Temperature ($T$), exchange coupling constants ($J_1, J_2$), and the instability criterion $\chi_{SW}^{	ext{nem}}(T) > K$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on spin-wave theory for magnon descriptions and treats the exchange modulation ($\delta$) as a static coordinate in some minimization steps.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the shift of the free energy minimum from $\delta=0$ to finite $\delta^*$ upon heating, confirming the entropic origin ($\Delta f < 0$), and present phase diagrams showing the finite-temperature altermagnetic window.
paper_structure: The paper develops the free energy functional, derives the instability criterion based on thermal susceptibility, and then uses both analytical (VSWT) and numerical (SLMC) methods to map out the temperature-dependent phase diagram, confirming the entropy-driven nature of the transition.
why_interesting: The mechanism provides a clear, non-conventional route to magnetic ordering (altermagnetism) driven purely by thermal fluctuations and entropy, which is a key concept in understanding complex phase transitions in correlated materials.
